lawyer:
Khair Ezaz Maswood, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner 
Nirmalendu Deb, Advocate ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Rama Kanto Nath others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Md Helal Uddin Chowdhury and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order of remand dated 29-6-1997 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Moulvibazar in Title Appeal No. 45 of 1991 should not be set aside or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The petitioners as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 22 of 1988 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Baralekha, Moulvibazar praying for a decree for establishment of title, for declaration that Kabala dated 11-6-1988 purported to be executed by the defendant No. 6 in favour of defendant No. 1-3 is void, collusive and without consideration and also for permanent injunction. Subsequently, by order dated 27-7-1989 amendment was allowed to the effect of recovery of possession of .01 decimal of land to the northern part of settlement plot No. 1260.

3. During pendency of the revisional application petitioner No.1 died and his heirs was duly substituted as petitioner No. 1(a)-1(c) by order of this court dated 6-10-2010.

4. The case of the petitioner in short, is that the suit land appertaining to settlement plot No. 1259 area 11 decimals and plot No. 1260 area 19 decimals including other land while was owned and possessed by Arjad Ali and Anjab Ali father of the defendant No.7. Mujahid Ali Chowdhury purchased the suit land including some other land by registered kabala dated 20-12-1951 corresponding to 6th Poush, 1358 BS of which item No.4 of the kabala schedule land attracts the suit land Mujahid Ali Chowdhury died leaving defendant No.7 in whose name the D.P. and final settlement khatian was rightly published and while defendant No.7 was in exclusive possession to sold away by two registered kabala dated 26-6-1978 and 25-10-1978 in favour of Priya Moni Debi, who transferred the same in favour of the plaintiff by deed of gift dated 8-9-1985 and 2-6-1987 and they are in possession of the said land by growing paddy and paying rents to the government. That the defendant Nos.1-3 obtained a collusive and fictitious kabala dated 11-6-1988 from one Sonahar Ali although their vendor or his predecessor had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. The plaintiff father came to know that the defendant No.7 during his father life time created a false lease deed dated 23-2-1954 in favour of the predecessor of the defendant Nos.4-6. Asab Ali, when the defendants threatened the petitioners to dispossess them from the peaceful possession in the suit land, they were constrained to file the present suit on 21.02.1989. During pendency of the suit, the defendants dispossessed the plaintiffs-petitioners from northern 01 decimal of land of suit plot No. 1260 for which they prayed for recovery of possession of the said land.

5. Defendants Nos. 1 and 2-opposite party Nos. I and 3 herein contested the said suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the defendants had no objection about the plaintiff's title in the 0.11 decimal of plot No. 1259 but regarding 0.19 decimals of land of plot No. 1260 the plaintiff case is that the total land of said plot is 0.35 decimals, same was owned by Mujahid Ali Chowdhury who for his financial crisis had leased out entire land of plot No. 1260 including other lands in favour of father of defendants Nos. 4-6 Asab Ali for a period of 10 years. It was stipulated in the leased that in case favour to return the money by the leaser within the specified period of the leased deed would automatically as complete sale and since then Asab Ali had been possessing the total land of plot No. 1260 within the knowledge of all concerned. In the last settlement operation name of Aftab Ali Chowdhury was wrongly inserted in the title column, but in the column of possession the name of Asab Ali was rightly recorded. After death of Asab Ali by amicable partition defendant No.6 Sanar Ali got the land of suit plot No. 1260 in his exclusive possession and sold it to the defendant Nos.1-3 by registered kabala dated 11-6-1988 since then they are in possession. During the war of liberation the original title deeds of the vendors of the answering defendants had been destroyed. With these averments the defendant prayed for dismissal of the suit with costs.

6. The trial court framed the following issues in the suit: a. Is the suit maintainable in its present form?

b. Have the plaintiffs any right, title, interest and possession in the suit land?

c. Were the plaintiffs dispossessed from the disputed 01 decimal of land?

d. Is the registered kabala dated 11.06.1988 without passing of consideration or a paper transaction?

e. Are the plaintiffs entitled to get the relief as prayed for or entitled to any other relief or reliefs?

7. Learned Assistant Judge after considering the evidence and materials on record decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 28-2-1991. Against the said judgment and decree the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 45 of 1991 in the Court of District Judge, Moulvibazar and on transfer it was heard and disposed of by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, First Court, Moulvibazar, who by the judgment and order dated 29-6-1997 allowed the appeal and sent the suit on remand to the trial court, on the finding that the local investigation is necessary for ascertaining the identity of the separate .01 decimal of land to entitle them to get a decree for recovery of khas possession of the suit land.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 29-6-1997 the plaintiff moved this court and obtained the present rule and stay.

9. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff petitioner submits that the learned Subordinate Judge committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in sending the suit on remand on his arbitrary reasoning that the local investigation of the suit land is required for effective determination of the suit. He further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge did not adverting to the fact that the suit land is specified by boundary in the plaint and in the absence of any objection from the defendants as to whether the specified land in plaint schedule attracts the land of the suit plot Nos. 1259 and 1260. He next submits that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge failed to consider the amendment of the plaint allowed the suit on 27-7-1989 before taking view that for effective decree of khas possession in 01 decimal of land local investigation was necessary. He finally submits that the learned appellate court misconstrue the exhibit-1, 3(ka) and 4 which bear sufficient identification and on proper perusal of the schedule of those kabalas attract the suit land of the plaint within the specified compact area and boundary.

10. He lastly submits that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge without applying his judicial mind referring to the admitted document exhibit-1 for the purpose of local investigation and for additional evidence under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

11. Mr Nirmalendu Deb, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendants-opposite parties submits whether the land describe in the schedule of the plaint is identical with the land described in the schedule 4 of the registered sale deed dated 20-12-1951(exhibit-1) but no issues was framed on this important point by the trial court whether the khatian or plot or boundaries in item No.4 land of the registered deed dated 20-12-1951 is identical with the suit schedule land. He further submits that defendant Nos. 1-3 at the earliest opportunity specifically raised preliminary objection in paragraph No. 10 of their written statement filed on 9-8-1989 that registered deed dated 20-12-1951 does not bear any khatian, plot or boundaries as that of the suit land. He next submits that although the trial court decreed the suit for '01 decimal for recovery of khas possession, but in the schedule of the plaint nothing was showing about .01 decimal land of plot No. 1260 which clearly shows that the total is 0.35 decimal out of which 0.19 decimal is the suit land. Although paragraph No. 19(kha) of the plaint was amended on 27-7-1989, but in the schedule of the plaint said .01 decimal of land has not been included, so the appellate court rightly remanded the suit for holding local investigation for ascertaining the said .01 decimal land. He also submits that since the suit land is vague, indefinite and unspecified the suit ought to have been dismissed by the trial court.

12. The appellate court after considering the materials evidence on record rightly remanded the suit for ascertainment of .01 decimal of land out of total 0.19 decimal of land of plot No. 1260. In support of his submission Mr Deb cited two decisions reported in 12 MLR (AD) 105 = 12 BLC (AD) 36 and 14 BLT (AD) 176.

13. Heard the learned Advocate of both the parties, perused the revisional application and exhibited documents filed by the parties and the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates.

14. It appears that the trial judge decreed the suit upon non-consideration of preliminary point and without considering objection raised by the defendant Nos. 1-3 in their written statement at the earliest opportunity for holding local investigation into the suit land and without holding such local investigation the plaintiffs are not entitled to get any decree in the suit as prayed for since the said objection directly hit at the root of the plaintiff's title in the suit. Further, the learned trial court did not consider the factual aspect of the case that no issues was framed whether the dag/plot in item 4 of the registered kabala dated 22-12-1951 attracts the suit schedule land or not.

15. It further appears that the suit land as described in the schedule of the plaint bearing dag Nos. 1259 and 1260 are unspecified, vague, indefinite and not clearly bounded and even the statements of the plaintiff are taken to be so far one block of the suit land as claimed by the plaintiff, but they failed to point out '01 decimal of land within the original boundary of the plaint from which the plaintiff alleged to have been dispossessed has not been specifically described with specific boundaries as such the plaintiffs are not entitled to get decree upon unspecified suit land without holding local investigation for ascertaining the identity of the suit land.

16. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the appellate court without adverting to the fact that the suit land is specified by the boundary in the plaint and in the absence of any objection of the defendant as to whether the specified schedule attract any land of the said plot No. 1259 and 1260. But it appears that the trial court totally failed to consider that the defendant's specific objection taken in paragraph 10 of the written statement and failed to give findings in this regard, so the question of adverting to the same facts does not arise at all.

17. It further appears that the kabala dated 22-12-1951 (Exhibit- 1) bears no khatian and dag number for identification and Exhibit-2 and 3 also bear unspecified land, but only described of two plots, quantum of land and boundaries which is not sufficient to decree the suit without holding local investigation. The appellate court while examining the judgment and decree of the trial court noticed that the plaintiff is admittedly out of possession of .01 decimal of land. But in the suit plaintiffs out of total area of 0.35 decimals claimed only 0.19 decimals of land and out of which they were dispossessed from simple '01 decimal of land and that there is no specification of land claimed by the plaintiff. Thus the trial court in passing a decree in favour of the plaintiff for unspecified .01 decimal of land was in error or in other words the decree passed by the trial court was not a legal one and the appellate court after considering the evidence and provision of law rightly set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and sent the case on remand to the trial court for holding local investigation.

<u>18. Law as in order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the plaintiff to give clear description of the land in suit so that the land in suit is identifiable. In the present case it is seen that the particulars of the land as in schedule of the plaint is vague and unspecified. In that state of the matter it is clear that the plaintiff have sought for declaration of title in respect of unspecified, vague and undivided land. If the land in suit is vague, unspecified and that relief sought is in respect of undivided portion of land of particular plot in that case suit for mere declaration of title is not maintainable.</u>

19. In the present case the learned appellate court rightly consider this aspect of the case and without dismissing the suit sent the suit on remand for ascertaining .01 decimal of land from which the plaintiff was dispossessed and sought for recovery of possession from that part of the suit land by holding local investigation.

20. It further appears that although the plaintiff amended his plaint, but failed to include the area of .01 decimal of land in the schedule of the plaint amended on 27-7-1989.

21. In that view of the matter I am of the opinion that the case should go back to the trial court for relaying of the suit for the purpose of ascertaining whether the land in suit of 1 decimal as stated in the schedule of the plaint from where the plaintiff was dispossessed by holding local investigation. In this regard reference may be made to the case of Nazrul Islam (Babul) vs Santi Rani Dhupi reported in 14 BLT (AD) 176.

22. In the background made above I find no merit in this revision.

23. Accordingly, the rule is discharged. The order passed by the Subordinate Judge now Joint District First Court, Moulvibazar is upheld.

24. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated. Send down the Lower Court Records and communicate the order at once.

End.
